Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test creates options using OptionBuilder and expects the option type to default to String.class if the type is not explicitly set (assertion on line 67). The current bug report confirms that getParsedOptionValue returns null unless the Option.type is explicitly set, meaning the default type is not String, but instead null or unset.

Inspecting OptionBuilder.create(char) shows it calls create(String) that instantiates a new Option with the given option string and sets its properties like longOpt, required, args, and importantly type (line 364). The Option constructor sets basic fields but does not set a default type (String or otherwise). The getType() method on Option simply returns the field type, which would be null if never set.

CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue uses getOptionValue to get a string representation and resolveOption to get the Option object. Then it calls TypeHandler.createValue passing the option's type. Since the type is null by default, the TypeHandler tries to parse the value using a null type and returns null.

Thus, the root cause is Option.type is null by default; there is no implicit fallback to String if the type is not set. This causes getParsedOptionValue to return null unless the user explicitly calls withType to set the Option type, as demonstrated in the test case. A fix could involve initializing Option.type to String.class by default, or CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue could default to String.class when Option.getType() returns null. This default behavior is currently not documented in javadoc according to the bug report.

In summary, the bug occurs because of lack of a default Option.type, leading to null return from getParsedOptionValue, contrary to user expectation that it would be String by default.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
